---
title: "About PPADEM"
subtitle: "Political Parties and Democracy in Africa"
---

**Political Parties and Democracy in Africa (PPADEM)** is an ambitious, collaborative multi-year research project investigating the role of political parties in shaping democracy across Africa. 

According to leading democracy watchdogs, political freedom across the continent has experienced significant challenges over the past decade. Observers often point to weak, clientelist political parties as primary drivers of this trend. However, some parties actively act to defend constitutional norms and strengthen democratic accountability. PPADEM investigates this variation through the largest empirical study of political parties ever conducted in Africa, analyzing **80 political parties** across **25 nations**.

The project is funded by an **ERC Synergy Grant** (2026–2032).

## Project Partners

- **[Afrobarometer](https://www.afrobarometer.org/):** Pan-African, non-partisan survey research network conducting regular public attitude surveys across 40+ countries.
- **[Jean Golding Institute](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/golding/):** University of Bristol’s central data science and AI institute.
- **[Bristol Digital Futures Institute (BDFI)](https://www.bristol.ac.uk/bristol-digital-futures-institute/):** Interdisciplinary institute researching the digital transformation of society.
